subject: Fishing view — Today's Fishing Forecast panel (renderFishingForecast) and its host renderFishing(), plus the scoring engine, for Lake Sequoyah
review_level: screen-component (the forecast panel), with one flow/IA finding on the whole Fishing view stack

user_context.primary_user: Paul, as an angler planning a Lake Sequoyah trip — deciding whether it's worth going and, if so, which window today. Mom (the make-or-break daily reader, reads at half-engagement / sometimes no glasses) is NOT the planner here, but she sets the legibility floor for anything that renders on the shared dashboard.
core_jobs_to_be_done: Decide: is it worth fishing Lake Sequoyah at all today? (go / no-go)
If yes: when today — which window is best?
Secondary: what's biting / how to fish it right now (per-species tactics)
user_context.context_of_use: A planning read, usually before heading out — at the house or on the property, ~0.3 mi from the on-site weather station whose data drives the estimate. Sometimes a quick mid-day glance. One-handed, often half-attended. Rural signal is weak (async data may be missing on first paint).
assumptions_made: Paul is the primary/only planner for the Fishing view; Mom reads the dashboard but likely does not use Fishing to plan a trip. The no-glasses legibility floor is applied as a shared-surface constraint, not as a claim Mom fishes. If Mom never opens Fishing, the legibility findings soften from 'important' toward 'nice-to-have'; if she does, they harden. Flagged as an open question.

No .user-research artifact exists for the Fishing JTBD specifically — user model is inferred from CLAUDE.md project tone + the anglers-plan-a-trip framing Paul supplied this session, not from validated fishing-use research.

The star rating labeled 'overall' is computed from largemouth-bass alone (compositeScore(..., 'largemouth-bass')); the inline comment says 'blended' but the code is not — read as a defect, not intent.

principles_applied: Typographic hierarchy by value (cross-project.md) — weight/size must encode informational value, not template position; applied here to grid-cell weighting, not just type
Make every surface read at half-engagement (fernwood.md) — worst-case one-handed no-glasses read sets the bar
Glyphs follow the journal voice, not the dashboard voice (fernwood.md) — traffic-light 🟢🔴 dots are ops-dashboard register
Tone-coherence across all chrome (fernwood.md) — tone is enforced on every surface (color, glyph, copy) or it doesn't hold
Field-journal / anti-urgency voice (Tate-Tracker CLAUDE.md 'Project purpose & tone' + content-principles) — no 'BITING NOW!' register
Icons earn their place — true AND useful (cross-project.md)
Meet the user at the action (cross-project.md) — lead with the decision, not a pile of facts
Model-read values are hypotheses until verified (global CLAUDE.md) — a computed estimate must not be laundered into apparent precision
Mom no-glasses accessibility (memory project_fernwood_mom_reading_accessibility) — meaning must be carried by size/color/position/icon, and small body copy + faint helper text are failures
Nielsen #2 match system & real world, #4 consistency & standards, #1 visibility of status, #8 aesthetic-and-minimalist design

findings.observation: The Fishing view shows TWO top-line verdicts that can disagree. The blue forecast panel leads with a live-conditions star rating (pressure + wind + moon + temp → 'Excellent Fishing'). Immediately below it, renderFishing() prints a second verdict — the '.fish-worth-bar' ('Prime fishing window at Sequoyah — Pre-Spawn Prime: …') — driven by a different engine (calendar worthFishing + historical-water-temp floor, not live conditions). Nothing reconciles them, so on a slow-pressure day the star can read 2/5 'Fair' while the worth bar right beneath it says 'Prime fishing window.'
findings.user_impact: Two authoritative-looking verdicts that contradict each other is the fastest way to lose Paul's trust in the whole surface — he can't tell which to believe, so he believes neither and falls back to his own gut, which makes the panel decoration. This is the trust-erosion logic of 'Static visuals lie on dynamic surfaces' applied to competing dynamic verdicts.
findings.principle_invoked: Meet the user at the action (cross-project) + Nielsen #4 consistency and standards
findings.recommendation: Pick ONE top-line verdict and let the two engines feed it rather than race it. The live-conditions score answers 'is today good' and the calendar/temp engine answers 'is this a good time of year' — fold them into a single lead (season sets the ceiling, today's conditions set where you land under it). Do not render two separate verdict blocks in the same scroll.

findings.observation: The panel leads with a 5-star 'overall' rating that (a) is actually bass-only despite the 'overall' framing, and (b) compresses five differently-trustworthy factors into one number. The two things a planner actually needs — go/no-go in words, and the best window today — are respectively implicit in the stars and buried below the 2×2 grid.
findings.user_impact: For a planning read the top-line question is 'worth going, and when?' A single star count is over-precise (implies the model can rank today 4 vs 3 out of 5) and under-explanatory (doesn't say go/no-go or when). Paul has to parse the whole panel to reconstruct the decision the lead should have handed him.
findings.principle_invoked: Meet the user at the action (cross-project); Typographic hierarchy by value — the most valuable content (verdict + window) should carry the most weight, not a decorative precision score
findings.recommendation: Lead with a plain-language go/no-go verdict and the single best window today ('Worth a morning cast — best light 6:10–7:20'). Keep a star or simple 3-tier badge as a compact glance-cue if Paul likes it, but demote it from headline to supporting. If a star stays, label it honestly (it's a bass read) or make it genuinely blended across the three species.

findings.observation: The 2×2 conditions grid renders water temp / pressure / moon / wind as four co-equal cells (identical size, border, weight). But these are not co-equal evidence: pressure trend and water temp are the strong bite drivers; moon/solunar is weak evidence; instantaneous wind is real but secondary. The grid's equal geometry asserts equal importance. The pressure cell also leaks ops-dashboard register (🟢 Great window / 🔴 Slow bite traffic-light dots).
findings.user_impact: Co-equal weighting quietly miseducates the planner — it teaches that a 'Peak lunar window' matters as much as falling pressure, when it doesn't. A user calibrating trust in the tool over time will notice moon 'predictions' miss and discount the whole grid, including the cells that are actually predictive. The traffic-light dots import a monitoring-app grammar that reads as 'alert' for a beat before the words resolve.
findings.principle_invoked: Typographic hierarchy by value (cross-project — extended from type weight to cell weight); Glyphs follow the journal voice, not the dashboard voice (fernwood)
findings.recommendation: Break the false equivalence. Give pressure + water temp the lead (larger, first, with the 'why'); demote moon + wind to a single quiet secondary line ('Moon: mild influence · Wind: 6 mph, favorable'). Do not give moon a quarter of the visual real estate. Strip the 🟢🔴 dots — carry pressure quality in the word ('falling — best bite window') and, if a cue is wanted, a small in-palette mark, never red/green.

findings.observation: Water temp is an ESTIMATE (estimateLakeTemp: air 7-day avg minus a 6–10° seasonal lag) but the pipeline launders it into apparent precision. A single '~58°F' picks exactly one phase band (getCurrentFishingPhase / waterTempScore) and that phase then anchors the whole panel (the overall sub-line, the water cell, the species phases). A ±2–3° model error — well within this method's noise — silently flips 'Pre-spawn prime' to 'Staging' and shifts the star count. The tilde is the only honesty signal, and it disappears at the phase/star layer. (Also: on first paint with no pressure history the placeholder still contributes score 12 to a confident-looking star.)
findings.user_impact: The estimate is presented as if measured. Paul plans a trip on a phase label that's really a guess dressed as a reading — exactly the 'model-read values are hypotheses until verified' failure the global rule guards against. When the lake doesn't match the label, the tool takes the blame for a certainty it never actually had.
findings.principle_invoked: Model-read values are hypotheses until verified (global CLAUDE.md); Nielsen #1 visibility of system status
findings.recommendation: Carry the estimate's uncertainty all the way through. Keep the tilde AND add a quiet 'estimated from air temp' signifier on the water cell (not just the lake badge). Where the estimate sits within ~2° of a phase boundary, hedge the phase ('warming toward pre-spawn') rather than asserting one side. Degrade the star honestly when an input is a placeholder (show 'building…' rather than a full rating on missing pressure data). Optional/high-value: sanity-check against the real measured water temp already in the app (USGS Etowah 00010, WEATHER_DATA.streamflow.waterTemp_F) or the on-site station — even shown as 'nearest measured' it grounds the estimate. (That last one is eng/data-layer adjacent — flagging, not designing it.)

findings.observation: Copy repeatedly breaks the field-journal / anti-urgency register. pressureTrend details: 'intense feeding burst, go now before it hits', 'best time to be on the water', 'toughest conditions of the cycle; go deep, go slow, or go home'. tempTips: 'Most aggressive feeding of the year', 'world-class fun', 'live minnow under a slip float is deadly'. Plus the 🟢🔴 dots in F3. This is fishing-magazine hype and 'BITING NOW!' urgency — the exact register CLAUDE.md's tone section rules out.
findings.user_impact: Urgency and hype are the tonal opposite of Fernwood's calm noticing voice; they fracture the gestalt the rest of the app protects. BUT note the real tension: the Fishing view has a different user (Paul-as-keen-angler, an instrumental job) than Mom-in-bed, so it can legitimately run warmer and more specific than the plant prose. The fix is to cut urgency and hype, not to drain the useful tactical specificity — 'squarebill on points, Senko on flats' should stay; 'go now before it hits' should go.
findings.principle_invoked: Field-journal / anti-urgency voice (CLAUDE.md); Tone-coherence across all chrome (fernwood). Consider routing the copy pass through content-steward.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the detail/tip strings in a calm keen-angler register: keep the concrete tactics, remove the countdown ('go now before it hits' → 'falling pressure — the most reliable bite of the cycle'), the bravado ('go deep, go slow, or go home' → 'tough, post-front — work deep and slow'), and the ad-copy superlatives ('world-class fun', 'deadly'). Drop the traffic-light glyphs.

findings.observation: Meaning-bearing text sits below the legibility floor and star meaning is encoded in near-identical golds. Sizes: .fish-fo-sub 11.5px, .fish-cond-sub 11px, .fish-cond-key 10px uppercase, .fish-sp-score-phase 9.5px. The star classes distinguish tiers only by subtle hue (s5 #c89000 amber vs s4 #b09020 vs s3 #7a9840 olive vs s2 #a09040 vs s1 gray) — differences invisible at a glance and meaningless to anyone not colour-parsing. The whole panel is also blue-on-pale-blue (#1a3a6a/#5a7a9a on #e4f0fc), lower contrast than the app's green-on-cream.
findings.user_impact: If Mom (or Paul mid-glance without glasses) reads this surface, 9.5–11px carries none of it and the star colour tiers are indistinguishable — meaning collapses to the filled/empty star COUNT alone, so the colour is doing no work while adding visual noise. Per the Mom-accessibility memo, small body copy and faint helper text are outright accessibility failures here.
findings.principle_invoked: Make every surface read at half-engagement (fernwood); Mom no-glasses accessibility (memory); Typographic hierarchy by value
findings.recommendation: Lift anything meaning-bearing off the sub-12px floor (kill 9.5px outright). Let star COUNT carry rating; either drop the per-tier gold micro-variation (one gold for filled) or, if a colour cue is wanted, use one clearly-different colour for 'poor/skip' vs 'good' — not five adjacent ambers. Reconsider the blue panel palette for contrast (see F9).

findings.observation: Known defects B + C, confirmed in code. 'Best windows today' renders Dawn (hard-coded first) → [solunar, async] → Dusk (hard-coded last), so order is by TYPE not clock — a 3am moonrise minor still renders after Dawn. The chips are colour-coded by type (dawn=yellow, dusk=orange, major=green, minor=blue) with NO legend, so the colours are unexplained. And no chip carries a bite-quality rank, so a weak-evidence solunar 'minor' looks equal to prime dawn light.
findings.user_impact: The one part of the panel that most directly answers 'when today' is the least legible: colours mean nothing without a key, the order doesn't map to the clock a planner reads by, and there's no signal which window is actually best. Paul can't scan it and pick a time.
findings.principle_invoked: Nielsen #4 consistency & standards (chronological is the expected order) + #1 visibility of system status; Icons earn their place — true AND useful (cross-project)
findings.recommendation: Render windows in true chronological clock order (merge dawn/dusk into the same sorted list as solunar, don't pin them). Rank each by expected quality (dawn/dusk light and falling-pressure overlap = best; solunar minors = weak) via a simple, legible cue — order + a one-word tag ('best' / 'good' / 'slim'), not four unexplained colours. If colour stays, it needs a legend; but a ranked chronological list with words needs no legend, which is the better fix. Weight dawn/dusk over solunar — solunar is the weak-evidence layer (ties to F3).

findings.observation: The Fishing view is one very tall dense stack with heavy intra-card duplication. Within a single scroll: water temp appears 4× (forecast cell, lake badge 'Est. now', temp-chart current dot, worth-bar context); phase label appears 4× (overall sub, water cell sub, worth bar, species phases); and the forecast panel's 'By Species' mini star-grid duplicates the species tabs + detail rendered just below it. Note 'Strip teases, card holds' permits strip↔card duplication — but this is all inside one card, so it's just repetition, not that contract.
findings.user_impact: Density without hierarchy makes the planning read slower, not richer — the signal (verdict + window) is diluted by the same three facts restated in five styles. For a half-attended glance the panel reads as 'a lot' rather than 'here's your answer.'
findings.principle_invoked: Nielsen #8 aesthetic-and-minimalist design; Meet the user at the action (cross-project)
findings.recommendation: Reorder to decision-first: (1) verdict + best window, (2) the two strong drivers with their 'why' (temp + pressure), (3) quiet secondary line (moon + wind), (4) per-species detail on demand. Collapse the forecast panel's species mini-grid into the existing species tabs below (one home for per-species, not two). Let the temp chart own the 'water temp' story so the other three restatements can shrink to a single lead.

findings.observation: The entire forecast panel is a blue weather-widget skin (linear-gradient #eef6ff→#e4f0fc, blue borders, blue text) dropped inside a green-on-cream field-journal app. It reads as an embedded ops/weather dashboard, not as a page of the journal.
findings.user_impact: Register-leak at the container level: before any copy is read, the blue widget signals 'app chrome / dashboard' rather than 'field notes on this lake,' undercutting the frame the rest of Fernwood works to hold. Compounds the glyph/tone leaks in F3 and F5.
findings.principle_invoked: Tone-coherence across all chrome (fernwood); Glyphs follow the journal voice, not the dashboard voice (fernwood)
findings.recommendation: Bring the panel into the Fernwood palette (warm cream/green, the app's card treatment) so the Fishing forecast reads as a page of the journal about the lake, not a bolted-on weather app. Water/lake can still get a cool accent, but as accent, not the whole skin.

open_questions_for_user: Does Mom ever open the Fishing view, or is it effectively Paul-only? This sets how hard the no-glasses legibility floor (F6) binds. My working assumption: Paul-only for planning, but it renders on the shared dashboard so the floor still applies as a shared-surface constraint.

For the single reconciled verdict (F1): do you want season to be a hard ceiling on today's live score, or should a great-conditions day be able to read 'good' even in a mediocre season? (i.e. which engine wins when they disagree, and by how much)

How warm should the Fishing voice run relative to the plant journal? I'm reading it as 'keen angler's log' — warmer and more tactical than Mom's plant prose, but still no urgency/hype. Confirm that's the register you want (it changes how far F5 goes).

The estimate-honesty fix (F4) can lean on real measured water temp (USGS Etowah 00010 / on-site station) — do you want that wired in as a calibration/sanity anchor, or is that out of scope for this UX pass?
follow_up_research_suggested: No fishing-specific JTBD artifact exists — a short user-researcher pass on how Paul actually decides a Sequoyah trip (what he checks, in what order, from where) would upgrade this review's user_context from medium to high and validate the 'lead with verdict + window' reorder.
content-steward pass on the pressureTrend detail + tempTip string bank (F5) — the copy rewrite is a voice job, not a UX one.

principles_to_propose.principle: Weight the surface by evidence strength, not by grid symmetry — a co-equal layout asserts co-equal importance
principles_to_propose.rationale: The 2×2 grid (F3) gives weak-evidence moon the same size/weight/border as strong-driver pressure. This is the same failure as 'Typographic hierarchy by value' but expressed through CELL geometry rather than type — equal tiles are a claim of equal importance, and when one tile is weak evidence the layout miseducates the user and eventually discredits the trustworthy tiles alongside it. Proposing this as an extension/companion to 'Typographic hierarchy by value': the rule governs not just font weight but any repeated component (tiles, chips, cells, stat rows) whose uniform geometry flattens a real hierarchy of confidence. Watch for a second occurrence (a stat strip, a chip row) before promoting from candidate.

principles_to_propose.principle: One surface, one verdict — don't let two engines race to the same headline
principles_to_propose.rationale: F1: the Fishing view renders two independent top-line verdicts (live-conditions star vs calendar/temp worth-bar) from two engines with no reconciliation, so they can openly contradict each other in the same scroll. Whenever two computations both produce an authoritative-looking judgment about the same thing, they must be composed into one before they hit the user, not displayed side by side — contradicting verdicts destroy trust faster than either being wrong alone. Plausibly generalizes (financial viewer: a rules-signal vs a model-signal; any dashboard with a 'status' plus a separate 'score'). Holds at one occurrence pending a second.
